Revised assessment: While the FOMC statement notes strong Q3 growth, a still-solid but moderating labor market, and an unchanged policy stance with a firm commitment to 2% inflation, both SLOOS and the Beige Book point to mounting headwinds. The Beige Book reports overall activity little changed to slightly down across Districts, softer consumer spending, easing labor demand and wage growth, and continued weakness in commercial real estate (with New York real estate contacts remaining pessimistic). It also highlights weaker loan demand, further tightening in lending standards, and some uptick in delinquencies from low levels—consistent with SLOOS findings of tighter C&I, CRE, and consumer credit tied to higher funding costs and wider spreads. Net: the outlook skews closer to neutral-to-slightly negative versus the prior modestly positive read, given broad credit tightening and softer District-level conditions despite a resilient banking system.
